items.headline: NSW opens ~$1.4m agtech grants for farmers inside the Central-West Orana REZ
items.summary: The NSW Government has launched a Smart Farming Program making about $1.4 million available to primary producers within the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone, with grants of up to $35,000 per producer covering 70% of the cost of eligible technology. Funded on the back of the REZ and announced by the Energy Minister around the National Renewables in Agriculture Conference in Dubbo (12 August), it targets productivity, efficiency, safety and resilience tools such as soil and water sensors, drones, livestock and crop monitoring, site security and fuel-tank sensors.
items.so_what: Directed agtech funding is another EnergyCo/NSW lever for demonstrating tangible landholder benefit in the state's most-advanced zone, and it lands while the upper-house inquiry's finding that REZ consultation gave communities 'no meaningful influence' is still fresh and the CWO roadshow is mid-run — making uptake, perceived fairness and whether farmers read it as genuine support rather than compensation for imposed transmission an early gauge of whether benefit programs are shifting rural sentiment ahead of the New England EIS exhibition later in 2026. Watch regional and farming-sector commentary (The Land, ABC regional, NSW Farmers) for the reception.
